understanding: Tracks that appear in more than 4 distinct playlists, with track name and playlist count.
edge_cases: two different tracks with the same name, each in 3 playlists (must not be merged)
reason: Groups by TrackId with COUNT(DISTINCT PlaylistId) > 4, handles the boundary and duplicate names correctly.

understanding: For each country, the customer(s) with highest lifetime spend (all ties), showing country, name and total.
edge_cases: countries with lower top than global max
expected: Aland A1 X 15.0; Bland B1 X 7.0; Cland C1 X 4.0; Cland C2 X 4.0
reason: The subquery takes the global MAX(total) rather than a per-country max, so only the overall top customer is returned.

understanding: Top 5 genres by revenue (UnitPrice*Quantity from InvoiceLine), descending, with revenue.
edge_cases: InvoiceLine price differs from Track price
track with NULL genre and large revenue
reason: Uses il.UnitPrice*il.Quantity, joins to genre, orders desc with LIMIT 5; matches on all edge cases.

understanding: Number of tracks in the playlist named 'Grunge'.
edge_cases: Grunge has 2 tracks while other playlists have more
reason: The query never filters on p.Name = 'Grunge', so it counts all playlist tracks.

understanding: Percent of total retail revenue contributed by each media type, rounded to 2 decimals.
reason: Numerator and denominator both use UnitPrice*Quantity from InvoiceLine; percentages match the hand calculation.

understanding: Artists with more than 10 albums, showing name and album count.
edge_cases: artist with 11 albums each with 1 track
reason: Joining Track and using COUNT(*) counts tracks, not albums, so an artist with 2 albums and 12 tracks is wrongly returned.

understanding: Count of artists that have never had any of their tracks sold, including artists with no albums.
edge_cases: artist with album but no tracks
artist with a sold track on multiple invoice lines
artist with one sold and one unsold track
track with NULL AlbumId that was sold
reason: NOT EXISTS through Album-Track-InvoiceLine correctly counts artists with no sales, including those with no albums.

understanding: Top 5 customers by total spend in year 2024, with name and total, descending.
reason: The query has no filter on InvoiceDate for 2024, so other years' invoices are included in the totals.

understanding: Top 3 genres by average track length in minutes (2 decimals), longest first.
edge_cases: genre with many short tracks (SUM vs AVG)
track with NULL genre and huge duration
4 genres with tracks so limit 3 matters
reason: AVG of Milliseconds / 60000.0 rounded and ordered desc with LIMIT 3 matches expectations, NULL-genre tracks excluded.

understanding: Percentage change of 2025 invoice revenue versus 2024, rounded to 2 decimals.
reason: Half-open date ranges include end-of-year timestamps with times and exclude neighbouring years; the result matches.
